title: Polish Thorun Confession: regenerate can lose true faith while in known sin
source_text: XXXVIII. Certe istud plane congruit cum doctrina Reformatorum in Regno Poloniae, ut manifestum facit eorum Confessio in Colloquio Thoruniensi exhibita. Falso, inquiunt, accusamur quasi statuamus semel justificatos, Dei gratiam, ejusve certitudinem, & ipsum Spiritum Sanctum non posse amittere, quamvis in peccatis pro lubitu volutentur, cum contra potius doceamus ipsos etiam renatos, quoties in peccata contra conscientiam recidunt, in iisque aliquandiu perseverant, nec fidem veram, nec Dei gratiam justificantem, nedum ejus certitudinem, aut Spiritum Sanctum, pro illo tempore, retinere; sed novum irae ac mortis aeternae reatum incurrere, ac propterea, nisi speciali gratia Dei excitante (quod in electis fieri non dubitamus) ad resipiscentiam iterum renoventur, reipsa etiam damnandos esse. Cap. 4. de Gratia. sect. 2. num. 11.
pass_a_gloss: Certainly this plainly agrees with the doctrine of the Reformers in the Kingdom of Poland, as their Confession exhibited in the Colloquy of Thorn makes manifest. Falsely, they say, we are accused as if we hold that those once justified cannot lose God's grace or certainty of it, or the Holy Spirit Himself, even while they wallow in sins at pleasure; whereas on the contrary we rather teach that even the regenerate, as often as they fall back into sins against conscience and persevere in them for some time, retain for that time neither true faith, nor God's justifying grace, still less certainty of it, or the Holy Spirit; but incur a new guilt of wrath and eternal death, and therefore, unless by God's special exciting grace (which we do not doubt happens in the elect) they are renewed again to repentance, are actually also to be damned (ch. 4 on Grace, sect. 2 n. 11).
pass_b_english: Polish Reformers at Thorn: false charge that the once-justified cannot lose grace while sinning at will.
Regenerate persevering in known sin retain for that time neither true faith nor justifying grace — new damnation-guilt unless renewed to repentance.

choices.why: Even the reborn can interrupt justifying faith.
